name: The Market Signal, Signal Ledger
rules: Every published or held finding gets an entry. Figures are recorded exactly as the source states them. Interpretations carry a confidence level (High, Medium, Low) and at least one checkpoint with an indicator, expected date, date status and owner. At each checkpoint the outcome is recorded as Confirmed, Partly confirmed, Not confirmed or Too early, with the evidence. Entries are never edited silently: every change is appended to the revision trail with a timestamp, author and reason.

entries.finding: U.S. apartment completions through Q3 2026 were about 231,000 units, 27% fewer than the same period of 2025. Q3 delivered a little over 82,000 units, the smallest third quarter since 2019.
entries.source: RealPage Analytics, U.S. Apartment Supply Update 3rd Quarter 2026, Oct 22, 2026
entries.verification: Verified on the publisher's page by Q and again by an independent fact checker, Oct 25, 2026
entries.local_evidence: Phoenix was among the five metros RealPage named for the most new deliveries in Q3 2026, each above 3,000 units, alongside Dallas, Houston, Austin and Atlanta. Partial: no verified public Phoenix rent, occupancy or concession figure.
entries.interpretation: National supply relief is real, but Phoenix is likely to feel it later than the national figure suggests.
entries.confidence_reason: One quarter of completion counts only; no verified local demand, rent or concession data.

entries.finding: U.S. rental vacancy was 7.6% in Q3 2026, higher than 7.3% in Q2 2026 and 7.1% in Q3 2025. West region 6.7% vs 6.0% a year earlier (significant). This came while RealPage counted 27% fewer completions through Q3 (Q3 rose from Q2).
entries.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership, Third Quarter 2026 (CB26-161), Oct 28, 2026
entries.verification: Read on the Census press release by Q and by an independent fact checker, Nov 1, 2026. Apartment List national and Phoenix pages read the same day. RealPage page re-read by Q.
entries.local_evidence: City of Phoenix median rent $1,250, down 2.5% over 12 months and 0.4% during October (Apartment List, November 2026 report); Chandler +0.7% fastest, Surprise -4.7% slowest in the metro. Limitation: no Phoenix or Arizona vacancy figure in this Census release; Apartment List figure is the city, not the metro.
entries.interpretation: Slower deliveries have not yet shown up as lower vacancy nationally, and the West's year over year rise suggests Arizona operators may face more choice per renter for a while before supply relief shows up in occupancy.
entries.confidence_reason: Census vacancy covers all rental housing and carries sampling error (plus or minus 0.3); one quarter; only local figure is a city level asking rent.

entries.finding: Yardi Matrix's September 2026 national report (Oct 19, 2026) says national renewal rent growth slowed to 1.7%, far below its 8.7% peak in early 2023, and turned negative in Phoenix (negative 2.4%) and Austin (negative 4.3%), while U.S. advertised asking rent growth improved to 0.7% year over year.
entries.source: Yardi Matrix, National Multifamily Market Report, September 2026, Oct 19, 2026
entries.url_note: This Yardi blog URL is reused for each month's national report; the September text was read Nov 8, 2026.
entries.verification: Read on Yardi Matrix's page by Q and by an independent fact checker, Nov 8, 2026 (exact quotes). Yardi Phoenix report and RealPage 3Q demand update read the same day.
entries.local_evidence: Yardi Matrix's Phoenix report for September 2026 (Oct 5) shows average advertised asking rents of $1,529, down 2.1% year over year and flat on a trailing three month basis; stabilized occupancy 93.2% in June, down 20 basis points year over year; 9,149 units completed in 2026 through July and 24,400 under construction. RealPage (Oct 6) says Phoenix's annual rent cuts narrowed to less than 2% and Phoenix saw rent growth in Q3. Limitation: Yardi's public page does not state the period or method behind the renewal figure; one month from one source; no Arizona figure beyond Phoenix and no verified Seattle figure this week.
entries.interpretation: In Phoenix, Yardi's renewal rent growth measure has turned negative while asking rents are flat over three months and down 2.1% over the year, which may mean residents are comparing renewal offers with what they can find advertised, so retention may depend more on how an offer compares with visible asking rents than on the size of the increase.
entries.confidence_reason: One monthly figure from one source; Yardi's public page does not state the period or method behind the renewal figure; no verified local renewal or retention data from operators.
